title: Billing Conditions for Long-Standing Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements: Late Fee Settlement
content:
**Condition 7.** For a late fee on an overdue invoice of a Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements agreement, the agreement's tenure is the number of whole calendar months from the agreement's approval date to the fee date. Tenure decides how the fee, computed to the cent from the unpaid amount past due and the late-fee rate, is settled:

- **(a) Tenure of 36 months or more:** the fee is divided by 2 and rounded down to the whole dollar.
- **(b) Tenure of 12 months or more and fewer than 36:** the fee is multiplied by 0.75 and rounded up to the whole dollar.
- **(c) Tenure of fewer than 12 months:** the fee stands as computed to the cent.

The settled fee is then set against the tier's minimum late fee, and the larger of the two is charged.

### Worked figures (hypothetical fee of USD 213.47 computed to the cent)

| Tenure at the fee date | Settlement | Settled fee |
|---|---|---|
| 40 months | 213.47 divided by 2 is 106.735, rounded down | USD 106 |
| 36 months | same as above | USD 106 |
| 35 months | 213.47 multiplied by 0.75 is 160.1025, rounded up | USD 161 |
| 12 months | same as above | USD 161 |
| 11 months | stands | USD 213.47 |

A fee of USD 40.00 at a tenure of 40 months settles at USD 20; on a tier whose minimum late fee is USD 25, the late fee charged is USD 25.

### Counting whole months (hypothetical dates)

An agreement approved on 15 January has a tenure of 35 whole calendar months on 14 January three years later, and of 36 whole months on 15 January three years later. An agreement approved on 15 January has a tenure of 11 whole months on 14 January of the next year and of 12 on 15 January of the next year.
